clue.text: Experts attempt to incorporate new blood

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take something into the body, so one word is set inside another

parts.note: aces are experts at something
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Specialists try to bring fresh people into a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood in the sense of lineage or descent, as in 'of noble blood', means family background.

clue.text: Initially amphibians stay on land

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: to shore up is to prop or stay something

explanation.surface: Frogs at first remain on dry ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on or to the shore, not at sea.

clue.text: Clergyman has a time in treatment

indicators.note: in places the pair of letters inside the remedy word

parts.note: a cure is a medical treatment

explanation.surface: A priest spends a spell in rehab.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant to a parish priest in the Church.

clue.text: Become suspicious when Pasternak heroine stuffs fish

indicators.note: stuffs means fills, so the heroine goes inside the fish

parts.note: the smelt is a small silvery fish
Lara is the heroine of Boris Pasternak's Doctor Zhivago

explanation.surface: Grow wary when a Russian novel's heroine crams a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is an idiom meaning to sense that something is wrong.

clue.text: Fear hooter is ill-fitted to make lots of noise

indicators.note: ill-fitted suggests parts badly put together, so the letters before it are reassembled

explanation.surface: A dreadful horn is badly fitted to a car making a din.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise the roof is an idiom for cheering or shouting very loudly.

clue.text: Motley collection causing little woman disgrace

parts.note: Jo March is one of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women
a blot on one's record is a disgrace

explanation.surface: A mixed bag of items brings shame on a young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' is not a general phrase but a nod to Alcott's novel Little Women, whose heroine is Jo.
explanation.definitionFit: A job lot is an assorted bundle of goods sold together at auction, a miscellaneous assortment.

clue.text: Australia's a gas!

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia; the 's is a link meaning 'is'
a means one

explanation.surface: An exclamation that Australia is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a gas' reads as slang for a lark, but gas is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule, found high in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Set about treatment of dilation

indicators.note: treatment means handling or processing, so the letters are worked over

explanation.surface: Begin a course of dilation therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone, past tense, is to attack them, physically or verbally.

clue.text: Edward keeps article about store for gunpowder, say

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the pieces go into the name

parts.note: Teddy is a pet form of Edward
a is the indefinite article
ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A man named Edward hides something near an explosives store.
explanation.walkthrough: Gunpowder is not the explosive but a green tea whose leaves are rolled into pellets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a small tin or box for keeping tea leaves, such as gunpowder.

clue.text: Dissident keeps motorway sealed

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a heretic dissents from established belief
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A rebel holds on to the main road, which is closed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermetic means airtight, completely closed so nothing gets in or out.

clue.text: Game prima donna made revealing tax protest

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game
a prima donna is the leading female opera singer, a diva

explanation.surface: An opera star staged a scandalous protest against taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the legend: Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry to make her husband lift a heavy tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the noblewoman rode unclothed through Coventry in protest at her husband's harsh taxes on townsfolk.

clue.text: Need lost ball replaced in sporting trophy

indicators.note: replaced means put in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A lost ball needs replacing during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lonsdale Belt is the championship award in British professional boxing.

clue.text: Mammal took food in both hands

indicators.note: in places the eating word between the two hand letters

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left, the two hands
to take food is to eat, past tense ate

explanation.surface: An animal ate holding its food in two paws.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, is a fierce African and Asian member of the weasel family.

clue.text: English drunkard getting Heather's deep secrets

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
Erica is the botanical genus of heather; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: An English boozer gets hold of a woman called Heather's private matters.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather reads as a woman's name, but it is the plant, whose genus is Erica.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are matters understood only by a small inner circle, hence arcane knowledge.

clue.text: Gold casket marked and scored

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a casket is a small chest
to mark work is to rate or grade it

explanation.surface: A gold box was graded and scratched.
explanation.definitionFit: Music that is scored has been arranged for the instruments of a band or ensemble.

clue.text: Performance needs overhaul when commander goes missing

indicators.note: goes missing means is absent, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: to recondition an engine is to overhaul it
CO is commanding officer

explanation.surface: A show must be revamped when the officer in charge disappears.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a performance or interpretation of a song or piece.

clue.text: Misleading promise to wear glasses

indicators.note: to wear puts the debt note inside the spectacles, which surround it

parts.note: specs are spectacles
an IOU is a written promise to pay

explanation.surface: An undertaking to put on spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious means plausible but false, deceptively attractive.

clue.text: Reasonable target in the coconut shy, say

definitions.meaning: someone legitimately open to attack or criticism
a coconut shy is a funfair stall where balls are thrown, a game at a fair

explanation.surface: Something fair to aim at at a fairground stall.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where coconuts are knocked off posts with thrown balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings fit: a legitimate object of attack, and literally an amusement at a funfair.

clue.text: Hypocrite makes bloomers in mournful song

indicators.note: in puts the flowers inside the lament

parts.note: a plaint is a lament
bloomers are things that bloom, flowers such as asters

explanation.surface: A two-faced person wears big underpants during a sad ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers suggests old-fashioned knickers; here it means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaster saint is a person who pretends to moral perfection, a sanctimonious pretender.

clue.text: Newsman travelled up without it

indicators.note: without means outside, so the reversed ride word surrounds the other
up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: A journalist came up from somewhere without it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' reads a word from the bottom; 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is the journalist in charge of a newspaper.

clue.text: A bird like this turned up over quarry

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from below upward

parts.note: so means in this way
quarry is hunted prey

explanation.surface: A bird looking like this flipped over its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes SO into OS, placed over PREY in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey.

clue.text: Drug for boy in erotic play

indicators.note: in places the boy among the rearranged letters
play signals that the letters are moved around freely

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A medicine needed for a lad in a racy stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erotic play' looks like a racy scene, but 'play' is the anagram signal and 'in' sets the lad among the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cortisone is a steroid hormone used medicinally to reduce inflammation.

clue.text: A key is allowed

parts.note: to let is to allow, past tense the same

explanation.surface: A key opens the way: it is permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Key here is not a lock tool but a low island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A key, or cay, is a small low island; an islet is likewise a little island.

clue.text: A river in Hindustan

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits within the word that follows

explanation.surface: A geographical fact: there is a river in northern India.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true, which is the joke: the river is also spelt out inside the place name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is the great river of Pakistan and northwest India, rising in Tibet.

clue.text: Charlie leaves boat for shrine

indicators.note: leaves means departs from, so the letter goes out of the vessel word

parts.note: a coracle is a small round boat
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man abandons a vessel to go to a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece an oracle was a shrine where a god was consulted, such as Delphi.

clue.text: Dicky to admire peacemaker

indicators.note: dicky means unsound or shaky, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Someone shaky looks up to a negotiator.
explanation.definitionFit: A mediator is a go-between who brokers settlement of a dispute.

clue.text: See Moor's scabbard

parts.note: s. is an old abbreviation used in references for 'see'
a moor is a heath; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: Look at the sword case belonging to Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: Moor's suggests Othello, but it is open moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is a close-fitting case for a blade, a sword holder.

clue.text: Artist tucked into meagre fish

indicators.note: tucked into places the painter inside the mean word

parts.note: meagre means scant, stingy
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter tucks into a skimpy fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: The stingray is a flat sea creature with a venomous barbed tail.
